newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court rejects plea to ban Miss World contest.
newsitem.headline: Indian court rejects plea to ban Miss World contest.

text.p: An Indian court on Friday dismissed a petition seeking a ban on this year's plans to stage Miss World in the southern city of Bangalore.
"It had no basis and the question of obscenity could only be assessed during the show and not before it," judge R.V. Raveendran said while dismissing the petition.
The petition was filed by the all-women Mahila Jagrana (Forum to Awaken Women) which said that beauty shows degraded women and were an insult to Indian culture.
The Indian media group Amitabh Bachchan Corp Limted (ABCL) said last month it had clinched the right to stage the Miss World contest.
Earlier this month, the Mahila Jagarna announced the formation of a 15-member "suicide squad" to stop the contest. The group has given no details of its planned tactics.
The right-wing, Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the state farmers' association also have said they oppose the beauty contest.
The student wing of the BJP staged a demonstration in the city on Friday against staging the Miss World contest. Police detained 61 people, including 21 women.
But Jayadevappa Patel, chief minister of Karnataka, the home state of Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, has dismissed the protests as propaganda and said the show would go on.
